subject: Lots of models on a small dataset: model quality, false discovery rate

messages.author: 3c04baa628d75472
messages.subject: Lots of models on a small dataset: model quality, false discovery rate
parts:
Dear All,

I am unsure whether my approach is sound so I would like to ask for your help.

Background:
I am trying to fit lots of models on a small life science dataset, see the code below.
Variables p1, p2, p3, s1 and s2 denote data.frames; p4 is a numeric vector; `year` is binary.

There are several issues. As measurements are quite costly, the number of observations will be capped at around 125, but relationships are complex. Most of the data.frames cannot be efficiently reduced in dimensions (lack of multicollinearity), so fitting a "global" model on NMDS scores or PCA PCs is not satisfactory - not to mention the issues with downstream biological interpretation. So, I thought of another approach.

Instead, I am trying to assess the relationships of selected individual features from these data.frames by building models in lavaan. The number of possible models (see expand.grid below) is 368676 (!). Lots of models typically fit very well (TLI.robust, RMSEA.robust). There is also non-linearity in the data (in part due to clr transformation).

# Script:

xpg <- expand.grid(
  s1 = 1:ncol(s1),
  s2 = 1:ncol(s2),
  p1 = 1:ncol(p1),
  p2 = 1:ncol(p2),
  p3 = 1:ncol(p3)
)

initmod_raw <- c(
  'p4 ~ year',
  'p4 ~ s1',
  'p2 ~ p1',
  'p2 ~ p3',
  'p2 ~ s2',
  'p2 ~ year',
  'p2 ~ p4',
  'p1 ~ s1',
  'p1 ~ s2',
  'p1 ~ p3',
  'p1 ~ year',
  'p1 ~ p4',
  'p3 ~ s1',
  'p3 ~ s2',
  'p3 ~ year',
  'p3 ~ p4',
  's2 ~ s1')

allmod <- foreach (j = 1:nrow(xpg), .combine = "rbind") %do% {
  cur <- data.frame(
    s1 = scale(s1[, xpg[j, 1]]),
    s2 = scale(s2[, xpg[j, 2]]),
    p1 = scale(p1[, xpg[j, 3]]),
    p2 = scale(p2[, xpg[j, 4]]),
    p3 = scale(p3[, xpg[j, 5]]),
    p4 = p4, # single column variable
    year = ifelse(year == 2020, 1, 0)
  )
   
  lavaanmod <- paste0(initmod_raw, collapse = "\n")
  fitmod <- sem(lavaanmod, data = cur, estimator = "MLR")
 
  # at this point, I simplify the model iteratively by elminiating the regression with
  # the highest p.value (if p.value > 0.05) from the model, in a for loop.
  # The loop breaks if the increase in rmsea.robust.pvalue is stopped, and a final model
  # is selected. This usually results in elimination of 3-7 regressions.
 
  sfm <- summary(finalmod, standardized=TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)
  sfm$fit
 
  # also collect weights for all models, not shown
}

quantile(allmod$chisq.scaling.factor, probs = seq(0, 1, .1))
#~        0%       10%       20%       30%       40%       50%       60%       70%
#~ 0.3844049 0.8419220 0.8801638 0.9072502 0.9307691 0.9526083 0.9750984 1.0003275
#~       80%       90%      100%
#~ 1.0322310 1.0832409 1.9845916

My questions are:
1. Literally tens of thousands of models have rmsea.robust == 0 & tli.robust >= 1. Clearly, some false discovery rate adjustment has to be used, for which my best guess currently is p.adjust(allmod$rmsea.notclose.pvalue.robust, "holm") or p.adjust(allmod$rmsea.notclose.pvalue.robust, "BH"). Would that be acceptable?

2. Several fits seem excellent, but even after iterative model simplification, there is a ratio of 1:5-7 (model parameter:observation), and there are also nonnormality issues. Is there a cutoff that can tell if the chosen models are simple enough to enable using sem() in the first place? E.g. Do I need an additional filter for models that are unreliable due to nonnormality? I was thinking of a chisq.scaling.factor filter (https://web.pdx.edu/~newsomj/semclass/ho_estimate2.pdf), but what about values smaller than 1?

Any thoughts and suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
